captures.name: exactly
captures.means: The literal word "exactly" when the step says the Owner halves exactly, and the empty string when it does not; it tells the body whether to pass --exact to the halve command, so an odd number's half keeps its half instead of being rounded toward zero.

captures.name: operation
captures.means: The operation the step names, either "halves" or "doubles", selecting which declared command of the calculator CLI the body runs: halve or double.

captures.name: number
captures.means: The step's whole number, with an optional leading minus sign so positive, zero and negative numbers are all captured; it is passed as the VALUE argument of the command.

definition.serves: The single clause of the Does: "Run the declared halve or double command, as the step names the operation, as a process with the step's whole number, passing --exact to halve when the step says exactly, and keep its stdout as the output." The operation capture serves "as the step names the operation", the number capture serves "with the step's whole number", and the exactly capture serves "passing --exact to halve when the step says exactly". The verb's plural s is part of the required wording "halves"/"doubles" that makes the step this concept, and the space before the operation is wrapped in a non-capturing group (?:...) because the presence of "exactly" alone, not its spacing, changes what the body does.
